# #4010: Patch (part 8 of 20): regression tests for JWT algorithm confusion and every claim the server checks
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

### What it does

Item 8 of #3897: **JWT algorithm confusion**. First-pass verdict: ✅ covered in code (`crates/server/src/auth.rs`):

- `decode_set` drops every symmetric (`oct`) key from the JWKS;
- `verify_against_jwks` refuses an HMAC `alg`;
- HS256 is checked locally only against a configured secret (`verify_against_secret`);
- `verify_options` requires `iss` and `aud`, and checks `exp` and `nbf` with zero leeway.

But no test holds any of this. `crates/server/tests/api/auth.rs` tests an HS256 token's `exp` and `nbf`, and nothing else in this list. Add tests that each of these is **refused**, both as a REST request and as a socket's token:

1. An HS256 token whose HMAC secret is the JWKS's own public key (the PEM, or the JWK's raw bytes): classic algorithm confusion.
2. A token with `alg: none` and an empty signature.
3. A token signed with an `oct` key the JWKS publishes (the JWKS harness at line 175 of `auth.rs` can serve one).
4. An ES256 token whose header is changed to say RS256, or HS256.
5. A well-signed token with the wrong `iss`, the wrong `aud`, no `iss` or no `aud`.
6. A well-signed token whose `kid` the JWKS doesn't publish.
7. With no HS256 secret configured, a forged HS256 token, refused once the provider says it doesn't know the token (the legacy path, `fetch_user_by_token`).

Use the existing harness (`GoTrue`, `es256_test_only.rs`). If a test fails, fix `auth.rs` and say so in the pull request.

### Acceptance

- The seven cases are tested over REST and the socket, and all are refused.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test api auth` and the whole-workspace gates green.

### Blocked by, part of

Part of #3897. Ticks #2629 §2's "confirm the server checks the signature, `iss`, `aud`, `exp` and the key id" once it merges.

### Difficulty (a guess)

medium: anything that is not hard

The night bot (bot:build)

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/tests/api/auth.rs` | change | New trailing module (helpers + 8 tests below); no other edit |
| `crates/server/src/auth.rs` | change only if a test fails | Fix the verifier; say so in the PR |

1. In `crates/server/tests/api/auth.rs`, append `mod jwt_forgeries_are_refused_over_rest_and_the_socket { use super::*; use crate::api::es256_test_only as es256; use crate::support::socket::{create_fake_socket, settle}; use jackioh_server::actor::ws_server::{WS_CLOSE, handle_match_socket}; }`. Name tests plainly (`refuses_…`); never cite a new `R…` number in a name or comment or `cargo jackioh spec check` fails.
2. Add helper `rest_status(app: &Arc<App>, token: &str) -> u16`: `call(app, "GET", "/api/auth/me", Some(token), Value::Null).await.0`, expecting 401 (copy the `call` destructure at line ~825).
3. Add helper `socket_close(app: &Arc<App>, token: &str) -> Option<u16>`: `let fake = create_fake_socket(); let half = fake.socket(); let uri: axum::http::Uri = "/ws/match".parse().expect("a uri"); handle_match_socket(app, &half, &uri, Some(token.to_string())).await; settle().await; fake.close_code()`, expecting `Some(WS_CLOSE.unauthorized)`. (`handle_match_socket` is `pub`; `authenticate_upgrade` is `pub(crate)` and unusable here.)
4. Add helper `seed_alice(app: &Arc<App>)`: `fake_of(app).lock().await.seed_profile(json!({"id": "profile-alice", "userId": ALICE, "status": "active"}))`. The socket never creates a profile (`upgrade_profile` returns `Ok(None)` → 4401), so every socket test seeds first: then 4401 can only mean the token was refused.
5. Add helper `b64url(bytes: &[u8]) -> String` via `base64::{Engine as _, engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD}` (`base64` is already a server dependency), and `sign_claims(gotrue: &GoTrue, user_id: &str, claims: Value) -> String`: unlike `sign` (which forces correct `iss`/`aud`), it sets only `sub` and `exp` (`FAR_FUTURE`) then HS256-encodes with `JWT_SECRET`.
6. Case 1 test: `Harness::new()`, serve the confusing key with `gotrue.answer_jwks(JwksReply::Serve(es256::jwks_body()))`; forge HS256 with secret `es256::TEST_ONLY_ES256_JWK_X.as_bytes()` (the JWK's raw bytes; the private PEM is not `pub`). Assert REST 401, socket 4401, and `(total, user_calls) == (0, 0)`: tier 1 drops Hmac headers before `keys_for`, tier 2 fails against `JWT_SECRET`.
7. Case 2 test: `none_token` = `format!("{}.{}.", b64url(header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}), b64url(payload with sub/iss/aud/exp))` on a default `Harness`. Assert 401 + 4401, no provider calls. (`decode_header` has no `none` variant, so tier 1 errs out; tier 2's `Validation` rejects it too.)
8. Case 3 test: serve `json!({"keys":[{"kty":"oct","k":b64url(b"attacker-oct-secret-1"),"kid":"attacker-oct","alg":"HS256","use":"sig"}]})`; sign HS256 with `b"attacker-oct-secret-1"` and correct iss/aud/exp. The oct secret must differ from `JWT_SECRET` or tier 2 accepts. Assert 401 + 4401, no provider calls (`decode_set` drops the `oct` key).
9. Case 4 test: take `es256::sign(&gotrue.issuer(), ALICE, claims)`, split on `'.'`, and re-emit with the header segment replaced by b64url `{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"es256-test-only"}` (same kid, original payload+signature), then again with `"alg":"HS256"`. Default harness. Assert both refused (401 + 4401, no provider calls): RS256 matches no published key's algorithm/family and is outside tier 2's Hmac list; HS256 dies at tier 1's family check and tier 2's signature check.
10. Case 5 test: four tokens via `sign_claims` — wrong iss (`"https://evil.test/auth/v1"`), wrong aud (`"evil"`), iss key removed, aud key removed (callers sets the other one explicitly). Default harness. Assert each 401 + 4401 with no provider calls (`verify_options` requires and checks both, leeway 0).
11. Case 6 test: build the no-secret triple inline (`GoTrue::start`, `Clock::new`, `supabase_auth_no_secret`; the `no_secret()` helper is private to the r1144000 module), serve `es256::jwks_body()`, forge with `es256::sign_with_kid("unknown-kid", &gotrue.issuer(), ALICE, claims)`. Assert 401 + 4401, `jwks_calls() == 1` (one fetch, miss answered from the fresh set), no provider calls. Premise in the same test: `es256::sign(...)` (known kid) verifies.
12. Case 7 test: no-secret triple as in step 11; `gotrue.answer_user(|_| UserReply::Ended)` (same-file call, as line ~841 does); forge HS256 with `b"some-unknown-secret"` and correct iss/aud/exp. Assert 401 + 4401, `user_calls() == 1` (the legacy `fetch_user_by_token` path ran) and `total() == 0` (no admin lookup).
13. Premise test `honest_tokens_still_pass_both_doors`: HS256 `h.token_for(ALICE)` → `h.auth.verify` ok and REST 200; then `seed_alice`, socket with the valid token → `Some(WS_CLOSE.not_found)` (4401 would mean auth failed; 4404 "you are not in a match" proves the token verified and only the match lookup failed). This guards the helpers against always-refuse.
14. Run the commands in Tests; if a refusal fails, fix `auth.rs` (not the test) and note it in the PR.
